source: Concise calibrations derived only from exact published comments in data/development_15_expectations.json.

anchors.guidance: A chair can be slightly pulled back or offset because chairs move. Treat a small but visible working-position mismatch as a review warning; reserve failure for a chair facing far away or a clearly unusable relationship.

Fail when a rectangular support table has visibly nonparallel or deformed side edges and is stranded implausibly in the middle of a home room. The printer can be correctly placed on the tabletop while the furniture anatomy and room placement still fail.
Do not require a movable chair to be in a perfect working pose. A modest offset is a review-level warning; a large incompatible facing or blocked approach can be material.

A rectangular or square home table can be implausible when left isolated in the middle of a room where a round freestanding table would make more sense. Judge support-furniture placement separately from printer-on-table placement.
In a close crop, an unseen chair may simply be outside the frame. Mark the user-position relation unobservable or as a warning for review rather than asserting that seating is absent.
Fail when visible furniture lacks legs or another credible load path required to support its tabletop. Inspect furniture anatomy even if the device itself contacts the surface correctly.
Fail a printer left with an implausibly large gap from the wall for its intended equipment-table scenario, even after allowing modest rear clearance for cables and ventilation.
A missing table leg or broken load path is a material failure. Do not let a minor chair-position concern distract from a larger furniture-anatomy defect.
Be lenient about small chair displacement. A mildly odd table angle can remain a warning while the overall placement passes when the device remains usable and the furniture is otherwise coherent.
Fail when the printer is visibly slanted relative to its support and an unrelated object is placed incoherently under the table. Inspect device-support axes and below-table prop logic independently.
A disfigured eyeglasses prop is a general rendering warning, not a natural-placement failure. Keep unrelated artifacts separate when device, support, access, and room placement are otherwise sound.

Fail when the support table sits implausibly in the room and a random object appears on the floor without a coherent use narrative. Both furniture layout and prop arrangement belong in the placement assessment.
Do not fail an otherwise usable laptop scene merely because a movable chair is not perfectly aligned. Minor chair variation can pass when approach and operating access remain credible.
